note: Authored crises. Each has a `when` predicate over facts the model already computes (see js/events.js FACTS), a `weight` for the draw, and two or three `options` whose `effects` come from a closed vocabulary. Nothing here invents a mechanic: every effect moves a number some other system owns, which is what keeps an event a nudge and a story rather than a second design.

events.title: The harvest fails
events.text: Two dry seasons in a row. The silos in {NATION} will not carry the winter, and the price of bread is already the only thing anybody is talking about.

options.label: Buy grain at any price
options.note: The treasury covers it. Nobody asks what it cost until later.

options.label: Let the market handle it
options.note: It will, eventually, and not to everybody.

events.title: A general will not go
events.text: The officer commanding {NATION}'s field army has written to say his men have been at this for years and he will not order them out again.

options.label: Relieve him
options.note: The army notices who was punished for saying it out loud.

options.label: Stand the army down
options.note: He was right, and everyone knows it.

options.label: Hear him out in public
options.note: An unusual thing for a government to do.

events.title: Shots on the border
events.text: A patrol strayed, or did not. Either way there are bodies on a line that {NATION}'s neighbours have been watching closely for some time.

options.label: Say nothing
options.note: The story will move on. The file will not.

options.label: Reinforce the line
options.note: Nobody crosses it again this year.

events.title: A petition for home rule
events.text: Half a million signatures, gathered in one quarter, asking that a region of {NATION} be allowed to govern itself. The organisers are careful to say they are not separatists.

options.label: Receive the petition
options.note: Which is not agreeing, and is not nothing.

options.label: Refuse to receive it
options.note: The signatures do not go away.

events.title: An offer from abroad
events.text: A consortium wants to build in {NATION} on terms that are generous and not entirely explained.

options.label: Decline
options.note: A government that cannot be bought is worth something.

events.title: The veterans march
events.text: They came from every part of {NATION} and they are camped outside the government buildings. Most of them are not angry, which is worse.

events.title: The currency slips
events.text: {NATION} has been spending what it does not have for long enough that somebody has noticed out loud.

options.label: Cut the army
options.note: The one line item large enough to matter.

events.title: A neighbour comes apart
events.text: The government next door has stopped governing. There are people at {NATION}'s border with everything they own.

options.label: Open it, and say what it costs

events.title: Where the money went
events.text: An auditor in {NATION} has found that a great deal of what was spent on the army did not reach it.

events.title: A convention is called
events.text: Enough of {NATION}'s regions have asked for it that refusing would itself be the answer.

events.title: They arrested the wrong person
events.text: A regional organiser was taken in for questioning in {NATION} and has not come out. The photographs are extremely good.

events.title: A good year
events.text: Nothing in particular went wrong in {NATION}, which has not been true for a while.
